result: concrete-minimal-seam-identified; no live UI/effect bitmap consumer qualified
scope: Trace retained CE HUD/interface bitmap and sprite selection to PS2 packet construction; distinguish BSP base material texture use from model OTEX coverage.

path: hud_draw_screen() [direct frame caller: interface_render() in source/interface/interface.c:728] -> hud_render_weapon_interface()/hud_render_unit_interface()/hud_render_nav_points()/hud_render_damage_indicators()
hud_retrieve_bitmap_and_bounding_rect(bitmap_group_index, sequence_index, frame_index, bitmap**, clip**) selects sequence sprite.bitmap_index and returns bitmap plus UV clip
hud_draw_bitmap_direct(bitmap, placement, point, clip, scale, theta, color, is_interface_bitmap) -> hud_draw_bitmap_internal(...) builds 4 dynamic_screen_vertex records with position, UV, color
findings.parameters: dynamic_screen_geometry_parameters contains bitmap_data *map[0], map scale/texture scale, point-sampling, blend; 4 vertices carry screen position, UV and ARGB color.
findings.host_callers: interface_render() directly calls hud_draw_screen() at interface.c:728. hud_draw_screen wraps HUD draws with rasterizer_hud_begin/end and invokes weapon, unit, nav-point and damage HUD. hud_draw.c element/number/meter callers resolve sprite bitmap and clip then call hud_draw_bitmap_direct/hud_draw_bitmap_with_meter. interface_draw_bitmap is an additional concrete call from hud.c for the multiplayer HUD marker. This is CE source call reachability; the inspected PS2 engine main.c does not call CE hud_draw_screen: its loop calls bsp_render_build(...), waits/presents and bsp_render_kick(...).
findings.reach: In CE game code, hud_draw_screen is reached from normal per-player interface/HUD frame flow; within this source slice it wraps its content in rasterizer_hud_begin/end. The inspected PS2 engine main.c does not call CE hud_draw_screen: its own loop calls bsp_render_build(...), waits/presents and bsp_render_kick(...). So source call reachability does not constitute an integrated PS2 runtime path.

findings.path: Thin dispatch wrapper to _rasterizer_psuedo_dynamic_screen_quad_draw. The definition is the Xbox D3D implementation in source/rasterizer/xbox/rasterizer_xbox_dynavobgeom.c, with global_d3d_device/D3D dynamic screen geometry calls; it is not a PS2 backend. The target-side executable clone is the declaration/dispatch source, not a target adaptation. PS2 GS packet builder lives separately in halo-ps2 engine/src/render/bsp_render.c and chain/upload/gs modules. No wrapper translating CE dynamic_screen_vertex + bitmap_data to the PS2 chain/GS texcache was found.
findings.minimal_implementation: Introduce a bitmap quad submission seam at the current PS2 frame-chain boundary: accept decoded/retained image descriptor or independently serialized bitmap handle, source dimensions, sprite UV rectangle, screen rectangle/rotation, tint/alpha, and blend mode; resolve a stable image key to texcache residency; emit 2 triangles with UV and color using existing chain/VU or direct packed GS sprite packet. Call it from an HCU screen-quad consumer implemented for this target, with a first test using one UI bitmap/sprite. Keep per-frame upload budget, deferred eviction rule (current/previous frame), and immutable snapshot data; do not route via the Xbox D3D function.

findings.path: Smallest proven CE geometry semantic is one textured quad; its exact arguments include bitmap, screen point, optional normalized clip/sprite UV, scale, rotation, fade. hud_draw_bitmap_direct adds placement semantics but resolves to the same 4-vertex draw. Reuse semantic input, not Xbox backend implementation.

world_load opens BSPn and TEXS/LMn for BSP material path; src_binding adapts object OTEX bindings. tex.c parses TEXS; bsp_render.c emits BSP GS draw packets. docs/09-tex-section.md defines TEXS as BSP lightmap-material base texture table; object/sky/particle/UI consumers are later scope; it explicitly calls out dropped BSP detail/bump/self-illumination/reflection maps. Object OTEX is separate from BSP TEXS.

The inventory says 987 bitmap records covered by model OTEX, 1,311 unsupported effect/sprite, 1,792 unsupported/unbound. A bitmap whose actual owner is an senv/sotr/schi/etc shader used by a structure BSP material can be bound through BSP TEXS and consumed by bsp_render; that does not require UI bitmap drawing and is not represented by the model_OTEX consumer label. Correct attribution needs owner shader tag id -> BSPS material shader_id crosswalk and TEXS binding, while retaining the genuinely unsupported cases (e.g. part/lens sprite owners and standalone UI roots). Current count labels alone do not prove every unbound record is a BSP material.

limitations: Source inspection only; no runtime HCP UI bitmap or sprite draw was executed.
No qualified HCP profile currently supplies UI/effect bitmap consumers; the existing UI profile attempt failed at media admission.
The PS2 compositor seam is an implementation proposal; no code or budget change is included.
The bitmap coverage inventory does not publish the BSP material shader-id crosswalk needed to reclassify the count definitively.
